papers.title_in_file: Antibunched Emission of Photon-Pairs via Quantum Zeno Blockade
papers.version_note: arXiv:1111.7018v1 (29 Nov 2011); the text is the paper its record names. The text layer drops some symbols (for example the inequality signs and approximate signs in Eq. (3)), and prints exponents flat.
papers.what_it_is: A theory and simulation letter proposing quantum Zeno blockade, via two-photon absorption, to suppress multi-pair emission in photon-pair sources, with a proposed microtoroid-in-rubidium-vapor implementation.

assertions.value: The authors define quantum Zeno blockade (QZB) as a mechanism that suppresses the creation of multiple photon pairs in a single spatiotemporal mode through the quantum Zeno effect, while the creation of a single pair is allowed. They state it is achieved by coupling the photon-pair system to a dissipative reservoir so that the coupling is efficient only when more than one pair of photons is present.
quotes: suppresses the creation of multiple photon pairs in a single spatiotemporal mode through the quantum Zeno effect [10], while the creation of a single pair is allowed.
It is achieved by coupling the photon-pair system to a dissipative reservoir in a way that the coupling is eﬃcient only when more than one pair of photons are present.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines QZB in its introduction (p.1-2).

assertions.value: The authors state that existing methods for deterministic entangled-photon generation rely on heralding, which requires a four-fold coincidence measurement or a two-fold coincidence measurement after nonlinear-optical mixing, and that the production rate of entangled photons is thereby fundamentally restricted to the sub-Hertz range.
quotes: a four-fold coincidence measurement [7, 8] or a two-fold coincidence measurement after nonlinear-optical mixing must be adopted [9].
the production rate of entangled photons is fundamentally restricted to the sub-Hertz range.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement about prior work, cited to other papers; no calculation is given in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that their model, a two-level ladder of pair-number states with an interaction Hamiltonian that has a real pair-generation efficiency, applies generally to nonlinear optical processes such as spontaneous parametric downconversion, spontaneous four-wave mixing and resonant two-photon superradiance. They treat the two-photon absorption (TPA) loss by a master-equation approach, and assume linear loss of the signal and idler photons is negligible compared to their nonlinear loss via TPA.
quotes: Such a model can be generally applied to a variety of nonlinear optical processes, such as spontaneous parametric downconversion (SPDC), spontaneous four-wave mixing (SFWM), and resonant twophoton superradiance.
the linear loss of the signal and idler photons is assumed to be negligible compared to their nonlinear loss via TPA.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own model and assumptions on p.2.
assertions.reader_inference: The model assumes negligible linear loss, so the results do not cover sources where linear loss matters.

assertions.value: The authors report that, for a TPA strength gamma (the sum of the signal and idler TPA coefficients) much larger than both the pair-generation efficiency Omega and the inverse of the effective interaction length L, solving the master equation approximately by adiabatic elimination gives a single-pair probability P1 of about sin squared of Omega L and a double-pair probability P2 of about (2 Omega / gamma) squared times P1, which is much less than P1 squared. They state this exhibits pair-wise antibunching. The text layer lost the comparison signs in this equation.
quotes: the system dynamics (2) can be solved approximately via adiabatic elimination
which exhibits the characteristic of pair-wise antibunching.
assertions.certainty_reason: The result is stated as an approximate solution with no derivation in the paper, and the text layer lost the operators of Eq. (3), so the full statement could not be quoted.
assertions.reader_inference: The derivation is not shown in this letter; the stated result rests on the authors' approximation.

assertions.value: The authors state that when TPA is sufficiently strong the vacuum state and the one-pair state form an isolated Hilbert sub-space, and that the transition dynamics corresponds to a Rabi oscillation between these two states, because the higher-order ladder transitions are suppressed.
quotes: When TPA is suﬃciently strong, the |00 and |11 states form an isolated Hilbert sub-space, and the transition dynamics corresponds to a Rabi oscillation between these two states.
assertions.certainty_reason: A qualitative statement about the model with no proof in the letter.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in the strong-TPA regime, when Omega L equals pi over 2 the probability to create a pair of photons is about one, and the probability to create multiple pairs is about 4 Omega squared over gamma squared, which is much less than one. They conclude that entangled photon pairs are then created directly with high fidelity, without heralding or other post pair-generation procedure. The text layer lost the approximate and comparison signs.
quotes: when ΩL = π/2 the probability to create a pair of photons is P1
is about 4Ω2/γ2
on-demand entangled photon pairs are created directly with high ﬁdelity, without the need for any post pair-generation procedure such as heralding.
assertions.certainty_reason: A consequence of the approximate Eq. (3), not proved separately; the printed form lost operators.
assertions.reader_inference: The 'high fidelity' wording is an author claim; the letter does not compute a fidelity.

assertions.value: The authors state that the pair-production rate can be very high, for example tens or hundreds of MHz, limited only by the bandwidth of the photon pairs, and that such rates would correspond to an improvement of more than ten to the seventh power (printed flat in the text layer) over those achievable via existing methods. The abstract states MHz rates or higher for the proposed microcavity implementation.
assertions.anchor: Section after Eq. (3), p.3; Abstract, p.1
quotes: The pair-production rate can therefore be very high, e.g., tens or hundreds of MHz, limited only by the bandwidth of the photon pairs.
Such rates would correspond to an improvement by more than 107 times over those achievable via the existing methods [7, 8].
assertions.certainty_reason: A projected rate from an idealized model; the letter itself notes that photon losses are not included and no experiment is reported.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is to heralded sources in the cited experiments and ignores the loss the paper says it defers.

assertions.value: The authors report numerical simulations of the master equation for the case in which only the signal photons are subject to TPA and the idler photons are not, which they expect is easier to achieve experimentally. The simulated ratios of gamma to Omega are 0, 3, 10 and 30, an increasingly stronger QZB effect.
quotes: we perform numerical simulations for the case with γb = 0, i.e., only the signal photons are subjected to TPA but not the idler photons
in (a)–(d) γ/Ω equals 0, 3, 10, 30, respectively, corresponding to an increasingly stronger QZB eﬀect.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the simulation setup on p.3.

assertions.value: The authors report that without TPA, the probability of multiple pairs is about the square of the single-pair probability P1 in the weak-pump regime, that it increases much faster than P1 when the pump power is increased, and that the two probabilities intersect at Omega xi of 0.9, where P1 is 0.25.
quotes: When the pump power is increased, Pn>1 increases much faster than P1. The two probabilities then intersect at Ωξ = 0.9, for which P1 = 0.25.
assertions.certainty_reason: A single simulation of the authors' model; the figure itself is not reproduced in the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors report that for gamma over Omega of 10, the simulation gives a single-pair probability of 0.6 and a multi-pair probability of 0.026 at Omega xi of 1.4, which they describe as a suppression of multi-pairs by 34 times below a typical non-antibunched result.
quotes: With γ/Ω = 10, as shown in Fig. 2(c), P1 = 0.6 and Pn>1 = 0.026 are obtained for Ωξ = 1.4, corresponding to suppression of multi-pairs by 34 times below a typical non-antibunched result [5].
assertions.certainty_reason: A single simulation of the authors' model.

assertions.value: The authors report that for gamma over Omega of 30, the simulation gives a single-pair probability of 0.83 and a multi-pair probability of 0.0036 at Omega xi of about pi over 2, which they describe as an ultra-strong pair-wise antibunching effect.
quotes: With γ/Ω = 30, as shown in Fig. 2(d), P1 = 0.83 and Pn>1 = 0.0036 are achieved for Ωξ ≈ π/2, establishing an ultra-strong pairwise antibunching eﬀect.
assertions.certainty_reason: A single simulation of the authors' model.

assertions.value: The authors state that adding TPA for the idler photons as well can significantly enhance the pair-wise antibunching effect. They also state that, comparing the four simulated cases, a stronger TPA channel increases the peak production rate of single photon pairs, which they attribute to enhanced QZB providing a better isolation for the Rabi-oscillation dynamics.
quotes: by introducing TPA for the idler photons as well (i.e., γb > 0), the pair-wise antibunching eﬀect can be signiﬁcantly enhanced.
for a stronger TPA channel, the peak production rate of single photon-pairs that can be achieved is increased.
assertions.certainty_reason: The idler-TPA case was not simulated in the letter; the peak-rate statement is an author reading of the figure.
assertions.reader_inference: The idler-TPA enhancement is stated without a simulated result in this letter.

assertions.value: The authors propose a device in which a Kerr-nonlinearity microring on a silicon pedestal is coupled to a tapered fiber, with the microcavity immersed in a rubidium vapor cell. The microcavity geometry is arranged for triple resonance and phase matching of the pump, signal and idler. The signal photon is at 778 nm, and the pump and idler are well detuned from Rb transition lines. TPA for the signal photons arises through evanescent coupling to Rb atoms near the ring surface, driven successively from 5S1/2 to 5P3/2 and from 5P3/2 to 5D5/2.
quotes: the microcavity geometry is arranged to achieve both triple-resonance and phase-matching for the pump, the signal, and the idler light waves.
we consider the signal photon to be at 778 nm, while the pump and the idler are well detuned from Rb transition lines.
excitations from 5S1/2 to 5P3/2 and from 5P3/2 to 5D5/2 are successively driven by two signal photons.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its proposed device and operating wavelength on p.4.

assertions.value: The authors state that cavities of this kind have been fabricated with ring diameters as low as about 50 micrometers and intrinsic quality factor well above ten to the eighth power (printed flat in the text layer). They state that, for a typical toroidal microcavity, a TPA coefficient on the order of gigahertz is obtainable using a Rb-atom density of about ten to the fourteenth per cubic centimetre, citing reference 28.
quotes: cavities of this kind have been fabricated with ring diameters as low as ∼ 50 µm, and Qi well above 108.
a large TPA coeﬃcient on the order of gigahertz is obtainable using a Rb-atom density of ∼ 1014/cm3 [28].
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited results attributed to other work (fabrication of toroidal cavities; Jacobs and Franson for the TPA coefficient).
assertions.reader_inference: The key gigahertz-scale TPA coefficient for the design rests on a prediction in the cited reference, not on a measurement in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that strong TPA in Rb vapors has been observed in hollow-core fibers and tapered fibers, and that it has been predicted that the TPA cross-section can be significantly increased by using the electromagnetically-induced transparency (EIT) effect.
quotes: strong TPA in Rb vapors has been observed in the system of hollowcore ﬁbers [26] and tapered ﬁbers [27].
it has been predicted that the TPA cross-section can be signiﬁcantly increased by using the electromagneticallyinduced transparency (EIT) eﬀect [29].
assertions.certainty_reason: Results attributed to other work.

assertions.value: The authors describe a counter-propagating scheme in which a pump pulse polarized at 45 degrees is split equally by a polarization beam splitter and sent around a fiber loop in both directions, so that clockwise and anti-clockwise pair-emission amplitudes are equal. The QZB suppresses simultaneous double pairs in the co-propagating or counter-propagating modes. The pairs recombine at the beam splitter into a polarization-entangled state, the equal superposition of the two pair states in the horizontal and vertical polarizations, up to a controllable relative phase.
quotes: a 45o-polarized pump pulse is passed through a polarization beam splitter (PBS) and split equally into horizontal and vertical components.
two photon pairs in copropagating or counterpropagating
modes, however, are suppressed due to the TPA-induced
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its proposed entanglement-generation setup on p.4-5.

assertions.value: The authors report that deterministic creation of entangled pairs in the proposed system can be achieved for root two times Omega times tau of about pi over 2 with gamma much larger than Omega. For gamma of 2 GHz, Omega of 0.1 GHz and tau of 10 ns they obtain a single-pair probability P1 of 0.74 and a double-pair probability P2 of 0.014. For gamma of 10 GHz, Omega of 0.1 GHz and tau of 11 ns they obtain P1 of 0.94 and P2 of 0.0005.
quotes: For realistic γ = 2 GHz
Ω = 0.1 GHz obtainable with an appropriate pump power, and τ = 10 ns achieved by adjusting the microring-ﬁber coupling, the probability to create a single pair of entangled photons P1 is 0.74.
The probability to create double pairs P2, on the other hand, is only 0.014
for γ = 10 GHz, Ω = 0.1 GHz and τ = 11 ns, P1 = 0.94 and P2 = 0.0005 are obtained.
assertions.certainty_reason: Model estimates for assumed parameter values, with no experiment, and without loss.
assertions.reader_inference: These are computed from the idealized model for assumed device parameters, not measurements of a built device.

assertions.value: The authors state that the actual pair-production rate obtained in practice could be lower due to photon losses, for example intrinsic cavity loss, fiber-cavity coupling loss and single-photon scattering by the Rb vapor, and that the detailed effects will be presented elsewhere.
quotes: the actual pair-production rate obtained in practice could be lower due to photon losses arising from, for example, intrinsic cavity loss, ﬁber-cavity coupling loss, and singlephoton scattering by the Rb vapor
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit on p.5.
assertions.reader_inference: The headline rate and fidelity figures therefore exclude the loss channels the authors name.

assertions.value: The authors state that although QZB relies on a strong coupling between multiple pairs of photons and a reservoir, when it is in effect ideally no energy dissipation or quantum-state decoherence will actually occur, as the creation of multiple pairs will be inhibited.
quotes: ideally no energy dissipation or quantum-state decoherence will actually occur as the creation of multiple pairs will be inhibited.
assertions.certainty_reason: An idealized author claim with no calculation of the residual dissipation.
assertions.reader_inference: The word 'ideally' limits the claim; the simulations do not report the residual dissipation.

assertions.value: The authors state that dipole blockade and photon blockade result from coherent energy-level shifting created by real potentials, caused by dipole-dipole interaction and vacuum Rabi splitting respectively, whereas QZB is realized through energy-level broadening produced by an imaginary pseudo potential caused by an incoherent, dissipative TPA process.
quotes: result from coherent energy-level shifting created by “real” potentials
QZB is realized through energy-level broadening produced by an “imaginary” pseudo potential caused by an incoherent, dissipative TPA process
assertions.certainty_reason: A conceptual distinction asserted by the authors, with a detailed comparison deferred to their reference 19.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that they have proposed QZB for overcoming the stochasticity of light scattering in nonlinear media and have shown that antibunched photon pairs in correlated or entangled states can be created deterministically at MHz rates or higher in a practical microring-cavity system. They list as applications deterministic entanglement swapping with linear optics only, ultra-bright single-photon sources via heralding, and quantum-key distribution with a substantially higher fresh-key-generation rate.
quotes: we have shown that antibunched photon-pairs in correlated or entangled states can be created deterministically at MHz rates or higher in a practical microring-cavity system.
deterministic (non-post-selected) entanglement swapping performed using only linear-optical instruments, ultra-bright singlephoton sources via heralding
assertions.certainty_reason: The conclusion rests on simulation and estimates only; no experiment is reported and the applications are listed without evaluation.
assertions.reader_inference: The word 'shown' refers to model results, not an experimental demonstration.
